bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Subtract the lines
bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
Choosing $3$ of the $9$ cells gives $\binom93=84$ placements. Exactly $8$ of them form a line (3 rows, 3 columns, 2 diagonals). So $84-8=76$.

**Answer: 76**

bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Write the sum in digits
bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
With $N=\overline{ABC}$, $N+\text{rev}(N)=101(A+C)+20B$. The possible cube sums are $125,216,343,512,729,1000,1331,1728$ (sums of two three-digit numbers, at most $1998$). Working mod $20$ gives $A+C\equiv$ cube mod $20$, so $A+C=5,16,3,12,9,0,11,8$ respectively; $A+C=0$ is impossible.

Since $20B\le180$ adds at most $1$ to the hundreds digit of $101(A+C)$, the hundreds and units digits of the cube must be equal or differ by one in the appropriate way; only $343$ with $A+C=3$ survives. Then $20B=343-303=40$, so $B=2$, and $(A,C)\in\{(3,0),(2,1),(1,2)\}$ ($A\ge1$): $N=320,221,122$. Sum: $663$.

**Answer: 663**

bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Computer check
bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
Testing all $N$ from $100$ to $999$ finds exactly $122,221,320$.

**Answer: 663**

bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: Generational means gcd with 2025 is 1
bmt-2025-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
The sums $\sum nc_n$ reach every residue iff $\gcd(\gcd(T),2025)=1$, i.e. iff the elements of $T$ have no common factor with $2025$ other than $1$ (by Bezout, if $\gcd(t_1,\dots,t_m,2025)=1$ one can reach $1$, hence every $j$).

So $T$ is not generational iff $\gcd(t_1,\dots,t_m,2025)=d>1$, i.e. every element is a multiple of some divisor $d>1$ of $2025$. The largest such set takes all multiples of the smallest such $d$, namely $d=3$: $\{3,6,\dots,2025\}$, of size $675$.

**Answer: 675**
